decisions.reason: As a core extension of the firm's established airfield control business with no clear negative signal and ample growth and R&D slack, it is likely to stay on the market.
The surveillance display fits the integrated airport-operations portfolio and, absent evidence of strong underperformance, management would likely continue it while learning from the market.
Training programs support the installed base and customer relationships, so even if demand is still developing the firm has enough slack to retain it.

This narrower training course appears less prominently supported than the other launches and is the easiest standalone offer to discontinue or fold into broader services if results fall short of aspiration.
Collaboration software is closely aligned with the firm's stated direction toward integrated, real-time and collaborative airport operations, which raises tolerance for short-term uncertainty.
Because it was presented as a flagship product in a strategic growth area, management would be especially reluctant to drop it unless performance were clearly far below aspiration.
